concerns.text: The plan simulates `review_effort_duration` for synthetic LLM PRs by sampling from an empirical KDE conditioned on the same five covariates used for propensity‑score matching (LOC, complexity, repo activity, semantic similarity, CI time). This makes the validation target (review effort) a deterministic function of the predictors, creating a circular/tautological validation: the synthetic outcome is drawn from the human outcome distribution conditioned on the covariates, so any subsequent test of “LLM vs. human review time” is guaranteed (by construction) to find no difference or only artefactual differences. This undermines the primary hypothesis and renders the statistical test non‑informative.

Step 5 states: “simulate a plausible `review_effort_duration` for synthetic PRs by sampling from an empirical KDE conditioned on the five matching covariates.” Because the same covariates are later used for matching and for the statistical comparison, the outcome is not independent of the predictors, violating a core requirement for causal inference and making the hypothesis test circular.
